facts.label: Contrary evidence and what would change the view
facts.text: The company reported compliance with all debt covenants at September 30, 2026 and says cash generated from operations and revolver availability are expected to meet operational needs, contractual obligations and debt service over the next twelve months. That evidence moderates near-term liquidity concerns, but it does not quantify covenant cushion; disclosed thresholds step down over time, and the acquired debt remains exposed to refinancing well before the 2031 facility maturity. Actual agreement-defined ratios, permitted add-backs and lender calculations would be needed to show whether the reported compliance provides robust headroom. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_dlx.htm.jsonl, pages 20–21, 33, 46; 10-K_2025-12-31_dlx.htm.jsonl, pages 107–108

- The complete July 31, 2026 amended credit agreement and covenant certificate are not present in the pinned sources, leaving covenant-defined EBITDA, actual ratios and headroom, exact spreads and floors, and collateral exceptions unestablished; this restricts covenant and borrowing-cost analysis, severity High, and can be closed with the executed agreement and certificate. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_dlx.htm.jsonl, pages 19–21, 51 - The legal ranking and complete guarantor scope of the 2029 senior unsecured notes, 2029 senior secured notes and receivables securitization are not stated; only the two first-lien facilities have a stated rank, so these instruments are omitted from the ranked debt stack and structural-priority and recovery analysis remains limited, severity High, and can be closed with the indentures, security documents and guarantee schedule. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_dlx.htm.jsonl, pages 19–22 - The income statements present aggregate other income, net but do not separately state interest income, limiting the split between interest and other non-operating income, severity Low, and can be closed with a component disclosure. Basis: 10-K_2024-12-31_dlx.htm.jsonl, page 75; 10-K_2025-12-31_dlx.htm.jsonl, page 67; 10-Q_2026-09-30_dlx.htm.jsonl, page 3 - The Q3 adjusted EBITDA bridge prints a dash for non-controlling interest, so a full numeric bridge cannot be reconstructed without treating a non-stated component as zero; this limits the component reconciliation while the reported adjusted EBITDA remains stated elsewhere, severity Low, and can be closed with the numerical input. Basis: EX99.1_2026-09-30_dlx_exhibit991110420268-k-htm.htm.jsonl, page 7 - The scheduled December 2026 dividend is USD 0.30 per share, but aggregate payment amount and payment-date share count are not stated, so pro forma net debt and leverage cannot be calculated, severity Low, and can be closed with the declared aggregate payment or subsequent cash report. Basis: EX99.1_2026-09-30_dlx_exhibit991110420268-k-htm.htm.jsonl, page 2 - Pension and retiree-medical obligations have not been fully updated after FY2025; this limits current claim quantification and benefit timing, severity Medium, and can be closed with current plan obligations and benefit schedules. Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_dlx.htm.jsonl, pages 102–106; 10-Q_2026-09-30_dlx.htm.jsonl, pages 9, 18–20 - Multi-year supplier and service commitments were USD 225.0 million at December 31, 2024 and USD 210.0 million at December 31, 2025; no updated remaining amount is stated at September 30, 2026, limiting current fixed-commitment analysis, severity Medium, and can be closed with an updated commitment schedule. Basis: 10-K_2024-12-31_dlx.htm.jsonl, page 63; 10-K_2025-12-31_dlx.htm.jsonl, page 57; 10-Q_2026-09-30_dlx.htm.jsonl, pages 23–24 - The September 2026 balance sheet reports USD 75.3 million of non-current finance lease liabilities, but the current portion within accrued liabilities and the resulting total finance lease liability are not stated, limiting total fixed-obligation measurement, severity Medium, and can be closed with the current lease-liability split. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_dlx.htm.jsonl, pages 2, 23 - No factoring or supplier-finance program is disclosed in the searched annual and interim sources, so whether such arrangements affect debt or working capital is not established, severity Low, and can be closed by issuer confirmation or program disclosures. Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_dlx.htm.jsonl, pages 107–110; 10-Q_2026-09-30_dlx.htm.jsonl, pages 18–23 - Selected financial-statement dashes leave gain-on-sale and Q3 non-controlling-interest amounts unstated; interim statements do not separately present impairment; and some cash-flow lines are dashed or not separately presented, including the FY2024 acquisition payment, selected-period residual commission buy-out and acquired-asset holdbacks, and 9M 2025 debt issuance costs. These amounts cannot be reconstructed; severity Low, and they can be closed with period-specific cash-flow and income-statement detail. Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_dlx.htm.jsonl, pages 67–69; 10-Q_2026-09-30_dlx.htm.jsonl, pages 3–4 - Cash proceeds from equity issuance and share repurchases are not separately stated in the selected cash-flow statements, limiting historical financing comparison, severity Low, and can be closed with transaction-level cash-flow detail. Basis: 10-K_2024-12-31_dlx.htm.jsonl, page 91; 10-K_2025-12-31_dlx.htm.jsonl, page 91; 10-Q_2026-09-30_dlx.htm.jsonl, page 51 - Recorded litigation liabilities are described as not material but are not quantified individually for FY2024, FY2025 or September 2026, limiting exact contingent-claim measurement, severity Low, and can be closed with a reserve schedule. Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_dlx.htm.jsonl, page 112; 10-Q_2026-09-30_dlx.htm.jsonl, page 23 - The sources do not provide comparable all-other segment revenue or EBITDA after the segment presentation changed, and they do not separately report annual adjusted EBITDA margins, limiting trend comparison for these measures, severity Low, and can be closed with comparable historical segment data. Basis: 10-K_2024-12-31_dlx.htm.jsonl, pages 51, 105–106; 10-K_2025-12-31_dlx.htm.jsonl, pages 113–114; 10-Q_2026-09-30_dlx.htm.jsonl, pages 42–43; EX99.1_2026-09-30_dlx_exhibit991110420268-k-htm.htm.jsonl, page 5

facts.label: Contrary evidence and what would change the view
facts.text: The strongest counterweight to the ownership and governance limitation is the issuer's regular SEC reporting, audited annual financial statements, quarterly debt and liquidity disclosure, and reported compliance with its financial covenants at September 30, 2026. The amended credit agreement also reports maintenance tests and restricted-payment limits, which gives creditors some disclosed contractual guardrails. These facts improve public financial visibility but do not establish beneficial ownership, actual covenant headroom, basket usage, or sponsor willingness. A current beneficial-ownership schedule, board and shareholder-control disclosures, lender compliance certificates, acquisition-level EBITDA and funding reconciliation, and related-party payment detail would materially improve the governance and transaction assessment. Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_dlx.htm.jsonl, pages 64, 116–118; 10-Q_2026-09-30_dlx.htm.jsonl, pages 19–21

facts.label: Contrary evidence and what would change the view
facts.text: The strongest counterweight to the leverage and maturity risks is that Deluxe generated positive free cash flow, reported compliance with its maintenance covenants, retained cash and undrawn revolving capacity, and extended the first-lien facilities to 2031. Q3 revenue and adjusted EBITDA were higher than in the prior-year quarter, and the latest release raised full-year guidance. These points reduce the case for near-term liquidity distress, but do not remove refinancing concentration or prove acquisition returns. Sustained organic growth in payment and data activities, realized Celero synergies, lower net debt and disclosed covenant cushion would improve the view; renewed Print weakness, weaker cash conversion or increased borrowing would worsen it. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_dlx.htm.jsonl, pages 19–21, 33; EX99.1_2026-09-30_dlx_exhibit991110420268-k-htm.htm.jsonl, pages 1–2, 4–7, 9; Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A)

facts.label: Credit view
facts.text: Deluxe's creditor case rests on a broad mix of merchant processing, B2B payment services, data activities and Print, with positive cash generation and a publicly reported compliance record. The principal constraint is that a large acquisition lifted debt before the acquired business has shown a sustained earnings contribution, while declining Print revenue remains a counterweight to the faster-growing service segments. Immediate liquidity is supported by cash and remaining revolving capacity; the larger risk is refinancing a concentrated maturity schedule without adequate leverage reduction. The business profile is adequate for a leveraged issuer, but financial flexibility is more limited than FY2025 because debt rose and acquisition execution remains incomplete. This view would strengthen with lower net debt, sustained free cash flow and evidence of realized synergies. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_dlx.htm.jsonl, pages 12–13, 19–21, 24, 43; EX99.1_2026-09-30_dlx_exhibit991110420268-k-htm.htm.jsonl, pages 1–2, 9; Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A)

facts.label: Company description and operating model
facts.text: Deluxe Corporation is a publicly traded, U.S.-centred provider of merchant payment processing, B2B treasury and payment services, data and marketing solutions, and checks, forms and promotional products. Its consolidated results combine transaction-linked service activity with a physical-product business exposed to secular substitution. Merchant, B2B and Data Solutions revenue depends on merchant and bank relationships, transaction activity, customer marketing demand and continued access to networks and data; Print depends on order volumes, product mix, paper, fulfillment and delivery. This combination spreads revenue across different end markets, but the mature Print business remains large enough that its decline can offset service growth. No individual customer exceeded 10% of reported revenue in the latest nine-month period, though this does not establish broad customer retention or pricing power. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_dlx.htm.jsonl, pages 24, 26–27; 10-K_2025-12-31_dlx.htm.jsonl, pages 29–34; Business & governance (CP-1A)

facts.label: Revenue, pricing and competitive position
facts.text: Competitive rivalry is relevant because payment processing, data and print services face alternatives and price competition; pressure on fees or retention can reduce contribution margins and cash available for debt service. Entry by technology-enabled providers could weaken merchant or bank relationships, although the filings do not quantify competitor shares or switching rates. Electronic payment methods are a direct substitute for checks and forms, creating structural Print volume pressure. The reported absence of a customer above 10% reduces single-name concentration, but bank partners and payment networks remain important intermediaries. Supplier and outsourced-service dependence, together with paper, postage, technology and delivery costs, can compress margins if pricing does not adjust. That creates offsetting growth and decline paths within the same consolidated cash pool. Regulation and privacy rules can affect payment processing, fraud controls and permitted use of data, raising compliance costs or constraining Data Solutions activity. facts.label: Issuer-specific downside scenario
facts.text: A plausible downside is a faster fall in Print orders combined with slower merchant growth and delayed Celero customer retention or synergy delivery. Lower Print volumes would weaken fixed-cost absorption; weaker service activity would remove part of the offset, while integration and acquisition costs would persist. Lower EBITDA and working-capital cash conversion would reduce free cash flow, leaving less cash for interest, amortization and debt reduction. Revolver drawings could rise to fund operations, reducing liquidity headroom as the 2029 maturities approach and increasing reliance on refinancing. Management could reduce discretionary capex, adjust costs, prioritize integration and moderate distributions, but the supplied disclosures do not establish enough fixed-cost flexibility or debt-repayment capacity to quantify how far these levers would protect cash. Current cash and revolver access support resilience, but there is not enough evidence to conclude that it would remain sufficient under a prolonged combined decline; this scenario does not assume default. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_dlx.htm.jsonl, pages 4–5, 19–21, 24, 26–27, 43; EX99.1_2026-06-30_dlx_tm2621737d1-ex99-1-htm.htm.jsonl, page 1; Financial foundation (CP-1)

facts.label: Overall credit view
facts.text: Overall, Deluxe presents an adequate business profile supported by payment and data activities, a broad customer base and positive free cash flow, but credit quality is constrained by secular Print decline, higher acquisition-funded debt and refinancing concentration. Cash-flow durability is adequate at present because operating cash generation remains positive, although working capital, issuer adjustments and integration costs limit its predictability. Refinancing capacity is likely to depend on Celero retention and synergy delivery, Print stabilization, sustained free cash flow and debt reduction before the 2029 maturities. The primary downside path is weaker Print and service activity alongside delayed acquisition benefits, which would pressure cash generation and increase refinancing reliance. Further analysis would require disclosed segment retention and pricing, cost sensitivities and acquisition-level earnings evidence. tables.title: Credit view — Metric
tables.limitation: Deluxe's creditor case rests on a broad mix of merchant processing, B2B payment services, data activities and Print, with positive cash generation and a publicly reported compliance record. The principal constraint is that a large acquisition lifted debt before the acquired business has shown a sustained earnings contribution, while declining Print revenue remains a counterweight to the faster-growing service segments. Immediate liquidity is supported by cash and remaining revolving capacity; the larger risk is refinancing a concentrated maturity schedule without adequate leverage reduction. The business profile is adequate for a leveraged issuer, but financial flexibility is more limited than FY2025 because debt rose and acquisition execution remains incomplete. This view would strengthen with lower net debt, sustained free cash flow and evidence of realized synergies. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_dlx.htm.jsonl, pages 12–13, 19–21, 24, 43; EX99.1_2026-09-30_dlx_exhibit991110420268-k-htm.htm.jsonl, pages 1–2, 9; Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A) The operating comparisons show positive Q3 adjusted EBITDA growth and nine-month free cash flow improvement, alongside lower nine-month revenue; the mix matters because Print pressure continues while service activities expand. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_dlx.htm.jsonl, pages 3–5, 12, 24, 43; EX99.1_2026-09-30_dlx_exhibit991110420268-k-htm.htm.jsonl, pages 4, 7, 9 The September balance sheet shows substantial cash and revolver access, but debt and scheduled maturities make liquidity quality dependent on preserving facility availability and refinancing before the bond wall. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_dlx.htm.jsonl, pages 19–21; Financial foundation (CP-1)

## Findings
### Bottom line

Deluxe’s September 2026 credit profile reflects substantially higher debt following the Celero acquisition, while reported cash generation and adjusted EBITDA remain positive; creditors therefore face greater leverage and a concentrated 2029 refinancing wall despite meaningful committed revolver availability. Covenant compliance is stated, but actual covenant ratios and headroom are not disclosed.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_dlx.htm.jsonl, pages 19–21; EX99.1_2026-09-30_dlx_exhibit991110420268-k-htm.htm.jsonl, pages 4–7; calculation ND26; calculation LTM-EBITDA; calculation LTM-AEBITDA
### Key findings

The July acquisition and related amended financing took gross principal debt to USD 2025.5 million and carrying debt to USD 2004.1 million at September 30, 2026. Net debt was USD 1929.2 million after deducting only unrestricted cash; this basis excludes separately presented finance and operating lease liabilities and does not deduct restricted settlement cash. The acquisition therefore increased leverage even as issuer-adjusted LTM EBITDA reached USD 459.8 million.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_dlx.htm.jsonl, pages 12, 19–20; EX99.1_2026-09-30_dlx_exhibit991110420268-k-htm.htm.jsonl, page 5; calculation ND26; calculation LTM-AEBITDA

At September 30, 2026, cash of USD 74.9 million and undrawn committed revolving capacity of USD 189.8 million provide a USD 264.7 million liquidity pool before future operating needs. The facility availability is already net of USD 9.7 million of letters of credit. The debt ladder is weighted to 2029 and 2031, and the source does not provide the covenant-defined EBITDA needed to calculate headroom against the maintenance tests.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_dlx.htm.jsonl, pages 19–21; calculation LIQ26; calculation MAT26

Nine-month operating cash flow and free cash flow were USD 215.9 million and USD 134.9 million, respectively, but they include working-capital movements and precede the USD 642.9 million acquisition outflow. Settlement processing obligations declined by USD 256.9 million in financing cash flow; this is a non-debt operating float movement and should not be read as debt repayment. Restricted cash was USD 19.3 million at September 30, 2026 and is unavailable for net-debt offset under the issuer’s stated definition.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_dlx.htm.jsonl, pages 4–5, 10; EX99.1_2026-09-30_dlx_exhibit991110420268-k-htm.htm.jsonl, pages 5, 9; calculation FCF9M26; calculation WC9M26
### Contrary evidence and what would change the view

The company reported compliance with all debt covenants at September 30, 2026 and says cash generated from operations and revolver availability are expected to meet operational needs, contractual obligations and debt service over the next twelve months. That evidence moderates near-term liquidity concerns, but it does not quantify covenant cushion; disclosed thresholds step down over time, and the acquired debt remains exposed to refinancing well before the 2031 facility maturity. Actual agreement-defined ratios, permitted add-backs and lender calculations would be needed to show whether the reported compliance provides robust headroom.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_dlx.htm.jsonl, pages 20–21, 33, 46; 10-K_2025-12-31_dlx.htm.jsonl, pages 107–108

The strongest operating counterweight is growth in the payments and data businesses and higher consolidated adjusted EBITDA, including Celero from its July closing date. The contrary pressure is continued Print weakness, acquisition-related amortization and financing costs, and non-recurring adjustment categories that may recur. Evidence that post-acquisition cash conversion and debt reduction persist after transaction costs and settlement-float movements would strengthen the operating case; lower growth, ongoing exceptional costs or weaker working capital would make the leverage increase more consequential.

## Findings
### Bottom line
Deluxe's operating model and Celero funding are assessable, but missing beneficial-owner and governance evidence prevents a decision-useful view of sponsor alignment and support for creditors.

The acquisition shifts more scale toward payments, while the issuer's filings do not establish final transaction economics, standalone acquisition earnings, or the owner's willingness to support debt.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_dlx.htm.jsonl, page 12; 10-K_2025-12-31_dlx.htm.jsonl, page 118
### Key findings

- The Celero acquisition materially increases secured borrowing while its all-in consideration remains only partly specified. The issuer reported approximately USD 625.0 million of cash consideration plus seller expenses and adjustments, USD 664.6 million of accounting consideration transferred, USD 21.7 million of acquired cash, and USD 642.9 million of net acquisition cash outflow. The net cash outflow reconciles to accounting consideration less acquired cash, but the issuer did not quantify the seller expenses and other adjustments separately.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_dlx.htm.jsonl, pages 12–13; calculation CELERO-CASH

- The amended first-lien facilities have meaningful remaining liquidity but increased the secured claim base. At September 30, 2026, the term loan facility was USD 800.0 million, the revolver commitment was USD 400.0 million with USD 200.5 million drawn, and USD 9.7 million of letters of credit left USD 189.8 million available. The filings say incremental term-loan and revolver borrowings funded the acquisition and its related costs, but do not allocate the acquisition funding between the facilities.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_dlx.htm.jsonl, pages 19–21

- Payment and data revenue growth offsets part of the secular decline in Print, but the segments have different demand and cost drivers. For the nine months ended September 30, 2026, Merchant Services, B2B Payments, and Data Solutions revenue totaled USD 854.5 million versus USD 745.7 million in the comparable period; Print revenue was USD 736.7 million versus USD 852.3 million. The newly acquired Celero operation contributed USD 33.5 million of revenue and a USD 1.9 million net loss after its July closing.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_dlx.htm.jsonl, pages 12–13, 24, 26–27; calculation SEGMENT-MIX

- Nine-month free cash flow was USD 134.9 million, based on USD 215.9 million of operating cash flow less USD 81.0 million of capital expenditures. Cash dividends paid were USD 43.0 million, while net cash used for acquisitions was USD 642.9 million; therefore, acquisition activity and debt financing, rather than organic free cash flow alone, drove the period's increase in capital needs.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_dlx.htm.jsonl, pages 4–5; calculation FCF-9M26

- Sponsor and governance risk is Insufficient Information. The issuer is a publicly traded company with regular audited and interim reporting and reported debt-covenant compliance, but its annual report refers beneficial-owner details to a proxy statement not included in the supplied source set and does not establish a sponsor, ownership percentages, board control rights, or sponsor economics.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_dlx.htm.jsonl, pages 1, 118; 10-Q_2026-09-30_dlx.htm.jsonl, page 20
### Contrary evidence and what would change the view

The strongest counterweight to the ownership and governance limitation is the issuer's regular SEC reporting, audited annual financial statements, quarterly debt and liquidity disclosure, and reported compliance with its financial covenants at September 30, 2026. The amended credit agreement also reports maintenance tests and restricted-payment limits, which gives creditors some disclosed contractual guardrails. These facts improve public financial visibility but do not establish beneficial ownership, actual covenant headroom, basket usage, or sponsor willingness. A current beneficial-ownership schedule, board and shareholder-control disclosures, lender compliance certificates, acquisition-level EBITDA and funding reconciliation, and related-party payment detail would materially improve the governance and transaction assessment.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_dlx.htm.jsonl, pages 64, 116–118; 10-Q_2026-09-30_dlx.htm.jsonl, pages 19–21
### Limitations

- The supplied filings do not identify beneficial holders, ownership percentages, sponsor fund terms, or board consent rights; this prevents a creditor-alignment or sponsor-support conclusion, while leaving the reported operating and debt facts usable.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_dlx.htm.jsonl, pages 1, 118

- Acquisition disclosures report different measures for Celero consideration and do not isolate final seller adjustments or standalone adjusted EBITDA; this prevents a complete purchase-price and acquisition-return assessment.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_dlx.htm.jsonl, pages 12–13; EX99.1_2026-06-30_dlx_tm2621737d1-ex99-1-htm.htm.jsonl, page 1

- The issuer reports covenant limits and compliance but not a current compliance certificate, actual covenant ratios, headroom, or basket utilization; this leaves creditor capacity and monitoring detail incomplete.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_dlx.htm.jsonl, pages 20–21
### Company and operating model

The segment disclosures show that Deluxe combines transaction and data services with a shrinking physical-product business; the mix and cost drivers create different paths for revenue durability and margin resilience.

### Transaction summary and new debt issues

Deluxe acquired all outstanding equity interests in Celero Commerce on July 31, 2026. The quarterly filing reports approximately USD 625.0 million cash consideration plus seller transaction expenses and other adjustments; the purchase-price allocation reports USD 664.6 million of consideration transferred. The acquired cash of USD 21.7 million reconciles that accounting measure to USD 642.9 million of net acquisition cash outflow. Seller expenses and adjustments are not separately quantified, so the difference between the approximate cash base and accounting consideration cannot be assigned more precisely.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_dlx.htm.jsonl, pages 12–13; calculation CELERO-CASH

The acquisition was funded through additional borrowing under the amended and restated credit agreement, using term-loan capacity and a revolver draw; the filing also identifies USD 15.4 million of related transaction costs for the first nine months of 2026. The amended agreement provides an USD 800.0 million first-lien term loan and a USD 400.0 million first-lien revolver, of which USD 200.5 million was drawn and USD 189.8 million remained available after USD 9.7 million of letters of credit. The reported maximum total-leverage test is 4.75x through June 30, 2027, 4.25x from September 30 through December 31, 2027, and 4.00x from March 31, 2028 onward; secured-leverage limits are 3.50x through December 31, 2027 and 3.25x from March 31, 2028 onward, while minimum interest coverage is 3.00x throughout. The issuer reported compliance at September 30, 2026, but did not publish actual ratios or headroom.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_dlx.htm.jsonl, pages 19–21

The September 30, 2026 principal debt schedule comprises the term loan, revolver drawings, USD 475.0 million of 8.0% senior unsecured notes due June 2029, USD 450.0 million of senior secured notes due September 2029 or earlier if the 2021 notes remain outstanding on February 1, 2029, and USD 100.0 million of receivables securitization obligations due December 2028 unless extended. The maturity schedule includes USD 15.0 million of term-loan amortization for the remainder of 2026, then quarterly installments. Total principal was USD 2,025.5 million before USD 21.4 million of unamortized discount and debt issuance costs. The first-lien credit facilities mature July 31, 2031; the term loan amortizes quarterly, beginning December 31, 2026. The maturity schedule is USD 15.0 million for the remainder of 2026, USD 60.0 million in 2027, USD 160.0 million in 2028, USD 985.0 million in 2029, USD 65.0 million in 2030, and USD 740.5 million in 2031. The receivables facility is classified as secured financing, with receivables serving as collateral.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_dlx.htm.jsonl, pages 18–22; calculation DEBT-PRINCIPAL

The acquisition release described expected scale and more than USD 15 million of expected cost synergies; the Q3 release said management was executing on integration synergy targets, while the accounting note says pro forma figures do not reflect integration or potential synergies. Celero contributed USD 33.5 million of revenue and a USD 1.9 million net loss in both the quarter and nine months ended September 30, 2026, including acquired-intangible amortization. This is initial contribution evidence, not proof of synergy realization or a full-year earnings run rate. ## Findings
### Bottom line

Deluxe has an adequate but more leveraged credit profile: service-business cash generation supports debt service, while Celero-funded borrowing, secular Print contraction and concentrated 2029 maturities constrain refinancing flexibility. Creditors have current liquidity, but the durability of acquisition returns and future deleveraging remains unproven.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_dlx.htm.jsonl, pages 12, 19–21, 24, 43; Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A)
### Key findings

Business mix partially cushions Print decline. Merchant Services, B2B Payments and Data Solutions expanded in the latest nine-month period while Print contracted; that service mix supports cash-flow diversification, but does not establish customer retention, price pass-through or a stable recurring-revenue base.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_dlx.htm.jsonl, pages 12–13, 24, 27, 43; Business & governance (CP-1A)

Leverage and refinancing are the central constraints. The Celero financing increased debt after a period of declining FY2025 net leverage, and reported net leverage reached 4.92x on an LTM reported EBITDA basis at September 30, 2026; USD 985.0 million of principal is scheduled in 2029, making access to refinancing and sustained cash generation consequential.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_dlx.htm.jsonl, pages 19–21; Financial foundation (CP-1)

Operating cash generation is positive but competes with other uses. Nine-month free cash flow improved year over year, yet acquisition cash outflow, dividends, debt amortization, working-capital variability and settlement-processing movements reduce the amount available for discretionary debt reduction.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_dlx.htm.jsonl, pages 4–5, 10, 19; EX99.1_2026-09-30_dlx_exhibit991110420268-k-htm.htm.jsonl, pages 2, 9; Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A)

Celero adds a potential growth engine and execution risk. Its post-close results do not yet demonstrate positive net earnings or realized synergies, so the acquisition's debt-service benefit remains uncertain. Public reporting is regular, but the supplied filings do not establish beneficial ownership or an equity sponsor whose support could be relied upon.

Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_dlx.htm.jsonl, pages 12–13, 118; EX99.1_2026-06-30_dlx_tm2621737d1-ex99-1-htm.htm.jsonl, page 1; EX99.1_2026-09-30_dlx_exhibit991110420268-k-htm.htm.jsonl, page 1; Business & governance (CP-1A)
### Contrary evidence and what would change the view

The strongest counterweight to the leverage and maturity risks is that Deluxe generated positive free cash flow, reported compliance with its maintenance covenants, retained cash and undrawn revolving capacity, and extended the first-lien facilities to 2031. Q3 revenue and adjusted EBITDA were higher than in the prior-year quarter, and the latest release raised full-year guidance. These points reduce the case for near-term liquidity distress, but do not remove refinancing concentration or prove acquisition returns. Sustained organic growth in payment and data activities, realized Celero synergies, lower net debt and disclosed covenant cushion would improve the view; renewed Print weakness, weaker cash conversion or increased borrowing would worsen it.

### Credit view

Deluxe's creditor case rests on a broad mix of merchant processing, B2B payment services, data activities and Print, with positive cash generation and a publicly reported compliance record. The principal constraint is that a large acquisition lifted debt before the acquired business has shown a sustained earnings contribution, while declining Print revenue remains a counterweight to the faster-growing service segments. Immediate liquidity is supported by cash and remaining revolving capacity; the larger risk is refinancing a concentrated maturity schedule without adequate leverage reduction. The business profile is adequate for a leveraged issuer, but financial flexibility is more limited than FY2025 because debt rose and acquisition execution remains incomplete. This view would strengthen with lower net debt, sustained free cash flow and evidence of realized synergies.

### Company description and operating model

Deluxe Corporation is a publicly traded, U.S.-centred provider of merchant payment processing, B2B treasury and payment services, data and marketing solutions, and checks, forms and promotional products. Its consolidated results combine transaction-linked service activity with a physical-product business exposed to secular substitution. Merchant, B2B and Data Solutions revenue depends on merchant and bank relationships, transaction activity, customer marketing demand and continued access to networks and data; Print depends on order volumes, product mix, paper, fulfillment and delivery. This combination spreads revenue across different end markets, but the mature Print business remains large enough that its decline can offset service growth. No individual customer exceeded 10% of reported revenue in the latest nine-month period, though this does not establish broad customer retention or pricing power.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_dlx.htm.jsonl, pages 24, 26–27; 10-K_2025-12-31_dlx.htm.jsonl, pages 29–34; Business & governance (CP-1A)

Deluxe's payments and data services can generate repeat transaction activity and leverage existing bank and merchant channels, supporting cash-flow visibility when customer relationships persist. The sources do not quantify contract terms, churn or price-volume splits, so the service base should not be treated as contractually recurring. Print demand faces ongoing electronic substitution and business process digitization; pricing and cost actions may slow the earnings decline but do not remove volume risk. The company relies on payment networks, bank partners, data access, vendors, paper and delivery services; disruption or adverse fee and cost changes can affect margins and operations.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_dlx.htm.jsonl, pages 29–34; 10-Q_2026-09-30_dlx.htm.jsonl, pages 24, 26–27, 43
### Ownership and group structure

Deluxe is publicly traded and files audited annual and quarterly reports. The supplied annual report points to proxy materials for beneficial-owner information, and the supplied filings do not identify an equity sponsor, controlling holder, ownership percentages or sponsor support. Accordingly, no creditor benefit from an owner backstop is assumed. Reported covenant compliance and recurring public reporting improve financial visibility but do not resolve ownership alignment or establish the amount of covenant capacity.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_dlx.htm.jsonl, pages 1, 118; 10-Q_2026-09-30_dlx.htm.jsonl, pages 20–21; Business & governance (CP-1A)
### Revenue, pricing and competitive position

Payment and data services are exposed to the volume of merchant transactions, bank-client activity, payment acceptance and marketing demand. Their growth in the reported period supports diversification and can partially offset Print, but the available evidence does not separate organic pricing from acquired volume, transaction growth or customer retention. Celero expands the merchant channel but was consolidated only from its closing date, so initial contribution is not a full-cycle measure of its durability.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_dlx.htm.jsonl, pages 12–13, 24, 27; EX99.1_2026-06-30_dlx_tm2621737d1-ex99-1-htm.htm.jsonl, page 1

Competitive rivalry is relevant because payment processing, data and print services face alternatives and price competition; pressure on fees or retention can reduce contribution margins and cash available for debt service. Entry by technology-enabled providers could weaken merchant or bank relationships, although the filings do not quantify competitor shares or switching rates. Electronic payment methods are a direct substitute for checks and forms, creating structural Print volume pressure. The reported absence of a customer above 10% reduces single-name concentration, but bank partners and payment networks remain important intermediaries. Supplier and outsourced-service dependence, together with paper, postage, technology and delivery costs, can compress margins if pricing does not adjust.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_dlx.htm.jsonl, pages 29–34; 10-Q_2026-09-30_dlx.htm.jsonl, pages 24, 26–27, 43
### Cost structure, margins and capital intensity

The segment cost base includes payroll, technology, merchant residuals, paper, outsourced production, shipping and delivery. This creates some operational flexibility through staffing, sourcing and production choices, but the filings do not quantify fixed versus variable cost shares or the amount of capex that can be deferred. If Print volume falls faster than costs can adjust, operating leverage can pressure EBITDA. Conversely, service growth and purchasing or integration efficiencies can support margins if retained without undermining service quality.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_dlx.htm.jsonl, pages 29–34, 55; 10-Q_2026-09-30_dlx.htm.jsonl, pages 26, 43

Nine-month operating cash flow less capital expenditures produced USD 134.9 million of free cash flow, compared with USD 95.9 million in the prior-year period. This supports debt service, but cash conversion includes working-capital movements and settlement activity; it does not represent cash freely available for debt repayment after interest, mandatory amortization, dividends and transaction costs. The company paid dividends and funded a large acquisition in the same nine-month period. The full-year 2026 guidance is management's outlook, not a cash-flow commitment, and no issuer cash conversion sensitivity is available for a downside case.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_dlx.htm.jsonl, pages 4–5, 10; EX99.1_2026-09-30_dlx_exhibit991110420268-k-htm.htm.jsonl, pages 2, 9; calculation 9M-FCF-CHANGE; Financial foundation (CP-1)
### PEST factors

Technology is a material credit factor: electronic payment adoption supports merchant processing, while digitization substitutes for checks and forms. That creates offsetting growth and decline paths within the same consolidated cash pool. Regulation and privacy rules can affect payment processing, fraud controls and permitted use of data, raising compliance costs or constraining Data Solutions activity. General economic conditions affect small-business transactions, bank-client activity and marketing budgets; weaker activity could pressure service volume and Print orders at the same time. The supplied evidence does not quantify these sensitivities, so no macro stress amount is assigned.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_dlx.htm.jsonl, pages 29–35; 10-Q_2026-09-30_dlx.htm.jsonl, pages 24, 27, 43

### Strengths and weaknesses

The principal credit strengths are a multi-segment platform, reported growth in payment and data services, positive free cash flow, committed revolver availability and regular public debt and financial reporting. These features support debt service and reduce dependence on any single customer or product, although revenue recurrence, cost flexibility and acquired earnings are not fully demonstrated.

The principal weaknesses are secular Print decline, higher post-acquisition debt, a concentrated refinancing wall, dependence on cash generation to reduce leverage and ongoing distributions to shareholders. Celero could add earnings scale, but until its contribution and synergies are evidenced, refinancing capacity remains sensitive to execution and operating performance.

### Financial profile and credit quality

Scale and breadth provide a meaningful operating base, and no individual customer exceeded 10% of revenue in the latest reported nine-month period. The market-position evidence is insufficient to claim leading share or a durable competitive moat. Revenue diversification is real at the segment level but weakened by the size and secular trajectory of Print. The available disclosures show positive consolidated adjusted EBITDA and free cash flow, but the measure includes issuer-defined adjustments and cash conversion remains exposed to working capital, transaction costs and settlement movements.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_dlx.htm.jsonl, pages 4–5, 24, 43; EX99.1_2026-09-30_dlx_exhibit991110420268-k-htm.htm.jsonl, pages 4, 7, 9; Financial foundation (CP-1)

Liquidity is supported by cash and an undrawn portion of a committed first-lien revolver, and the issuer reported compliance with its maintenance covenants. This is a positive near-term signal, but actual covenant ratios and headroom are not supplied. Refinancing capacity is constrained more by the bond and securitization schedule than by the July 2031 maturity of the bank facilities; the 2029 concentration leaves less room for delayed deleveraging. Financial policy includes recurring dividends and material acquisition activity. Ownership alignment and sponsor support are not established, so no external equity support is assumed.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_dlx.htm.jsonl, pages 19–22; EX99.1_2026-09-30_dlx_exhibit991110420268-k-htm.htm.jsonl, page 2; Business & governance (CP-1A)
### Outlook, tailwinds and headwinds

Over the next year or two, growth in merchant payments, B2B services and data, along with the planned Celero integration, could support revenue and adjusted EBITDA. The countervailing risks are ongoing Print contraction, execution costs, the acquired business's unproven earnings contribution and the need to preserve revolver availability while repaying scheduled term-loan amortization. Management raised its 2026 outlook after the third quarter, but the outlook is forward-looking and does not establish cash available for debt reduction.
Basis: EX99.1_2026-09-30_dlx_exhibit991110420268-k-htm.htm.jsonl, pages 1–2, 4–7; 10-Q_2026-09-30_dlx.htm.jsonl, pages 19, 24, 43

Over the next three to five years, further digitization could support payments and data but continue to erode checks and forms. The ability to sustain margins and free cash flow through this mix shift will determine whether Deluxe can reduce debt before the 2029 bond maturities. Continued synergies and customer retention in Celero could improve the refinancing case; failure to retain merchants or achieve integration benefits would leave a larger debt load against a weaker or stagnant Print base.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_dlx.htm.jsonl, pages 29–34; 10-Q_2026-09-30_dlx.htm.jsonl, pages 12–13, 19, 43; EX99.1_2026-06-30_dlx_tm2621737d1-ex99-1-htm.htm.jsonl, page 1
### Issuer-specific downside scenario

A plausible downside is a faster fall in Print orders combined with slower merchant growth and delayed Celero customer retention or synergy delivery. Lower Print volumes would weaken fixed-cost absorption; weaker service activity would remove part of the offset, while integration and acquisition costs would persist. Lower EBITDA and working-capital cash conversion would reduce free cash flow, leaving less cash for interest, amortization and debt reduction. Revolver drawings could rise to fund operations, reducing liquidity headroom as the 2029 maturities approach and increasing reliance on refinancing. Management could reduce discretionary capex, adjust costs, prioritize integration and moderate distributions, but the supplied disclosures do not establish enough fixed-cost flexibility or debt-repayment capacity to quantify how far these levers would protect cash. Current cash and revolver access support resilience, but there is not enough evidence to conclude that it would remain sufficient under a prolonged combined decline; this scenario does not assume default.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_dlx.htm.jsonl, pages 4–5, 19–21, 24, 26–27, 43; EX99.1_2026-06-30_dlx_tm2621737d1-ex99-1-htm.htm.jsonl, page 1; Financial foundation (CP-1)
### Issuer matrix synthesis

Revenue durability is adequate but exposed to secular Print substitution and unmeasured customer retention. Margin resilience is mixed because payments and data growth support earnings while Print volumes and input costs can pressure fixed-cost absorption. Free cash flow conversion is positive but includes working-capital variability and competes with dividends, acquisition costs and amortization. Liquidity is currently supported by cash and the revolving facility, while refinancing capacity depends on deleveraging and capital-market access before 2029. Financial policy and governance remain less assessable because beneficial ownership and owner support are not established in the supplied materials.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_dlx.htm.jsonl, pages 4–5, 12–13, 19–24, 26–27, 43; Business & governance (CP-1A); Financial foundation (CP-1)

Primary downside path: Print contraction and weaker service activity, combined with delayed Celero benefits, reduce cash generation and slow debt reduction before the concentrated 2029 refinancing requirement.
### Overall credit view

Overall, Deluxe presents an adequate business profile supported by payment and data activities, a broad customer base and positive free cash flow, but credit quality is constrained by secular Print decline, higher acquisition-funded debt and refinancing concentration. Cash-flow durability is adequate at present because operating cash generation remains positive, although working capital, issuer adjustments and integration costs limit its predictability. Refinancing capacity is likely to depend on Celero retention and synergy delivery, Print stabilization, sustained free cash flow and debt reduction before the 2029 maturities. The primary downside path is weaker Print and service activity alongside delayed acquisition benefits, which would pressure cash generation and increase refinancing reliance. Further analysis would require disclosed segment retention and pricing, cost sensitivities and acquisition-level earnings evidence.
